name: mee-table
author: Breed Art Studios

sections.description:
mee-table lets you accept table reservations from your own WordPress site, with a booking calendar, capacity per time slot and a confirmation email to the guest.

Free, with no account and no key. Reservations, the booking calendar, basic capacity, the confirmation email and events with ticket sales all run on your own WordPress, in your own database, using your own site email address. Nothing to sign up for, nothing to pay.

This is the Lite version, and it is free forever. With a mee-table account you also get prepayments and no-show protection (card or digital wallet), gift cards, the guest assistant, WhatsApp and SMS reminders, time-based discounts, staff accounts with the Waiter Dashboard, reports, and colours that match your theme. These run through the mee-table service at api.mee-table.com, so there is no server for you to maintain.

Every installation starts with a 14-day trial of the full version. When the trial ends the plugin does not switch off: it carries on at the free level, and your venues and bookings stay where they are.

What it costs, and what we take. The plugin is free. A mee-table account is from EUR 24 per month billed yearly (EUR 29 monthly), and there are higher plans for larger venues and groups.

We never take a commission on table reservations. Ever, on any plan, including the free one. A guest booking a table costs you nothing.

A percentage applies only where a ticket is sold and paid online: Dating Aperitivo tickets, Cooking Class tickets and gift cards. It is deducted at the moment of payment, and the rest goes straight to your own Mollie, Stripe or PayPal account. Mollie only opens accounts for businesses based in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the United Kingdom (list of countries); venues elsewhere, for example in the US, connect Stripe:

  • Free (or after the trial ends): 20% on Dating Aperitivo, 12% on Cooking Class, 10% on gift cards
  • Bronze: 15% on Dating Aperitivo, 5% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Silver: 12% on Dating Aperitivo, 3% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Gold: 10% on Dating Aperitivo, 2% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Platinum: agreed with you

On paid plans and during the trial the gift card percentage is capped at EUR 10 per card; on the free plan it is 10% with no cap.

Both percentages go down as you move up a plan: Dating Aperitivo from 20% on Free to 10% on Gold, Cooking Class from 12% to 2%. If you never sell a ticket, you never pay a percentage.

Main features:

  • Table reservations with availability, opening hours, rules on the number of guests, a weekly closing day and a quick-block calendar for one-off closures.
  • Guests manage their booking on YOUR site. The link in every email and message opens your own booking widget, on your own pages, in edit mode: the guest moves the date, the time or the number of guests, or cancels, inside the limits you set. A per-venue cap says how many people one booking may bring (the venue capacity is a separate number), and an optional notice window closes online changes some hours before the table, after which the guest is asked to call you.
  • Move a booking instead of losing it. The guest can change the day, the time or the number of people from the link in their confirmation email, without calling: the free tables are re-checked live, and you decide how many times they may do it before they are asked to phone you. Your own staff can move any booking from the Waiter Dashboard, with no limit, the phone rings there.
  • Your own time zone, so opening hours and reminders are right even when the venue and the server are in different countries.
  • Prepayment by time band. An “Aperitivo” rate from 19:00 to 20:00 and a different one for dinner, each with its own days of the week and minimum number of guests. The guest is only ever offered the rate that covers the time they picked, and when a rate covers it the prepayment replaces the no-show card guarantee: nobody is asked to pay twice for the same evening.
  • Sittings that change by day. For example 20:00, 21:45 and 23:00 from Friday to Sunday, and other times from Tuesday to Thursday. You type the start time you want, even 20:05. A sitting with no amount (for example Aperitivo 18:00-20:00, Dinner 20:00-22:00, After-dinner 22:00-24:00) only decides which times guests can book, and works on every plan, Free included and without a licence, because it is saved in your WordPress site. Prepayment amounts start from the Gold plan (or the 14-day trial).
  • Gift cards paid with Mollie or Stripe Connect, with a “Coming soon” preview per venue, a venue picker, one page per language with WPML or Polylang, and gifting to another person by email or WhatsApp.
  • Choose which emails reach you. Everything that happens to a booking sends you an email by default, confirmed, declined, cancelled or moved, including what your own staff did from the dashboard. Untick the ones you do not want; your guests keep receiving theirs either way.
  • No-show guarantee: the guest’s card is authorised, not charged. Nothing is taken unless they fail to turn up, and staff release or charge it from the Waiter Dashboard.

  • You decide what your staff can do. For each action on the phone dashboard (confirm, cancel, mark a no-show, refund a payment, waive a no-show charge) you choose all staff or the manager only. Until you change it, everything works as before.

  • Set menus at a fixed price, that guests book like a ticket: the whole thing happens on YOUR website, from the list of menus to the booking form, and only the payment page itself opens the payment provider’s own window, because they refuse to be shown inside a frame. You can ask for full prepayment, cap the seats per day or per service, and write each menu in as many languages as you like. The kitchen sees how many portions per service in the Waiter Dashboard.

  • Cooking classes, custom events and Dating Aperitivo, each with its own page on your site, its own photo, its own ticket and its own flyer to print.

External services

The city pages on mee-table.com (off by default)

Under mee-table, Events, Cooking Classes, Presentation there is a tick called “Show this class on the mee-table.com page for your city”. It is off unless you turn it on. With it on, the title, the description, the photo, the address and the next dates of your class appear on our public city page, for example https://mee-table.com/corsi-di-cucina/firenze, so people searching for a cooking class in your town can find you. Untick it and you are off that page at the next save. Nothing else about your venue is published.

This plugin relies on external services. Below is what each one is, when it is contacted, and what is sent to it.

1. mee-table backend (https://api.mee-table.com): always required

The plugin is a client for the mee-table SaaS. Every page of the admin and every booking talks to it. Data sent: reservation details (guest name, email, phone, number of guests, date, notes), location configuration, prepayment and gift-card records, staff accounts, and any photo you upload for a cooking class. Without this service the plugin cannot show availability, take payments or store bookings. Provided by mee-table. Terms: https://mee-table.com/terms | Privacy: https://mee-table.com/privacy

Two calls to the same provider happen outside the admin pages, and are listed here separately so it is clear when they occur:

  • Activating the plugin sends nothing anywhere. The first contact happens when you enter your licence key and press Activate: at that moment, once, the plugin asks https://mee-table.com/api/provisioning whether this domain already has a mee-table account, so the site connects to its own restaurant without anyone typing a token. Data sent: the site URL (get_site_url()) and nothing else. If it fails, the plugin simply carries on unconfigured. Until a licence key is entered, the plugin contacts no server at all.
  • Once a day, a scheduled task asks https://api.mee-table.com/api/license/validate whether the subscription is still active. Data sent: the site URL, the licence key the site owner entered, and the name of the product asking (mee-table), so a key bought for mee-class does not unlock bookings. How that data is handled: https://mee-table.com/privacy This call does not happen at all until a licence key has been entered: with no key the task returns immediately.

No guest data is involved in either of these two calls.

2. Payment providers: only when you enable and connect them

Mollie, Stripe or PayPal are contacted to create payments, authorise no-show guarantees and issue refunds. Data sent: amount, currency, reservation reference, and the guest’s payment details entered on the provider’s own hosted page. Card numbers never pass through WordPress. Mollie: https://www.mollie.com/en/user-agreement | https://www.mollie.com/en/privacy Stripe: https://stripe.com/legal | https://stripe.com/privacy PayPal: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/home

3. SMS providers: only if you choose one, and only for the messages you send

If you configure an SMS provider, your site sends the reminder text and the guest’s phone number to it. Two paths exist: reminders are dispatched by the mee-table backend, while the “Send test SMS” button sends one message directly from your own WordPress server to the provider, using the credentials you typed in. Nothing is sent to any of these companies unless you select them and save credentials. The panel also accepts a custom HTTP gateway: in that case the same two pieces of data go to the endpoint address you type in yourself, and to nobody else.

Twilio: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal Skebby (Commify Italia S.r.l.): terms https://www.skebby.it/wp-content/uploads/Contratto-SKEBBY.pdf | privacy https://www.skebby.it/wp-content/uploads/Informativa-Privacy-Estesa-SKEBBY.pdf Aruba SMS: https://hosting.aruba.it/documents/term_conditions/condizioni_fornitura_servizisms_aruba-it_v-1-2.aspx | https://www.aruba.it/documents/tc-files/it/11_it_privacy_policy_aruba_spa.aspx Brevo: https://www.brevo.com/legal/ Vonage: https://www.vonage.com/legal/ (its SMS endpoint is still the old brand name, https://rest.nexmo.com)

SMSGate (https://api.sms-gate.app): only if you choose the Android phone gateway

If you pick “Android phone” as the SMS route, your site does not talk to the phone directly: it sends the reminder text and the guest’s phone number to the SMSGate cloud at https://api.sms-gate.app/3rdparty/v1, which passes the message to the free SMSGate app on your own phone, and the message then leaves from your own SIM. This happens only for the messages you send, and only after you have installed the app and saved its username and password in the panel. SMSGate is an open-source project (the app is at https://github.com/capcom6/android-sms-gateway) and the cloud service is run by its authors.

SMSGate: https://sms-gate.app/terms-of-service/ | https://sms-gate.app/privacy/

A “generic HTTP” option exists for providers not in the list: there the endpoint is the one you type in, and you are responsible for it.

4. Meta / WhatsApp Business Cloud API (https://graph.facebook.com): only if you set up WhatsApp messages

If you fill in the WhatsApp fields of a location (phone number ID, WhatsApp Business Account ID and access token, all obtained from your own Meta Business account), your WordPress site talks to Meta directly in three cases, and never otherwise:

  • “Create the message templates on Meta”: reads the message templates that already exist on your WhatsApp Business Account and submits the missing ones for Meta’s approval. Data sent: the wording of the booking messages and your access token. No guest data.
  • “Send test WhatsApp”: sends one real confirmation message, filled with sample values, to the number you type into that field, to check the setup works. Data sent: that phone number, the sample values and your access token. No guest data.
  • The reminder texts themselves are fetched from https://mee-table.com/api/whatsapp/modelli, a public page of the mee-table site that only returns the wording of those messages. Nothing is sent to it.

The WhatsApp Business Account is yours: you own the number and you pay Meta directly. mee-table neither resells messages nor owns any number. Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-terms | Privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-data-processing-terms Meta Platform Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms | Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy

5. Mailchimp: only if you enter an API key

Used to add newsletter subscribers to your audience. Data sent: the email address and the consent flag of guests who opted in. https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/ | https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/

6. Groq: only if you enter a Groq API key for the guest assistant

Used by the guest assistant on your booking page. When a visitor types a question, that question is sent, together with your restaurant’s public information (name, address, phone, opening times, which time slots are still free in the next 7 days, discounts and events), to Groq, which produces the answer. The request is made server-to-server through the mee-table backend using your own Groq account, so the key never appears in a public page.

Never sent: names, phone numbers or e-mail addresses of your guests, and no booking of theirs. Free seats are counted; who booked them is not sent.

Nothing at all is sent to Groq unless you have entered a key in mee-table -> Guest assistant. Leaving that field empty keeps the assistant off and the script is not even loaded. Groq does not retain these questions for inference requests and is not permitted to use them to train its models.

Getting a key is free and takes about two minutes at https://console.groq.com/keys, the plugin explains the steps on that settings page. The Groq account is yours: the agreement for it is between you and Groq. Terms: https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/services-agreement Privacy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy Acceptable use: https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/ai-policy

Answers are generated by an automated system and can be wrong, and the assistant tells the visitor that it is automatic. Any answer containing a percentage is discarded before the visitor sees it. An answer containing an amount is discarded too, unless you have published prices on the pages you ticked and that exact figure appears there: the assistant repeats what you wrote, it never composes a price. On allergens it answers only by repeating what your own pages say, and any request for a guarantee about a guest’s own health is sent to your phone instead.

Privacy

This plugin sends reservation data, prepayment details, gift-card information, and location configuration to the mee-table backend at https://api.mee-table.com. If you enable the WhatsApp reminders, the guest’s phone number is also sent to Meta’s WhatsApp Business Cloud API so the message can be delivered, using the WhatsApp Business Account that belongs to you. The data is used solely to provide the booking service, payment processing, and no-show protection. No data is sold, shared with third parties for marketing, or used for advertising. If you enable the guest assistant, visitors’ questions and your restaurant’s public information are sent to Groq through your own Groq account, as described under External services above; no guest personal data is included. For full details, please read the mee-table Privacy Policy.

Retention: identifying data on a reservation (guest name, email, phone and notes) is irreversibly erased 180 days after the reservation date, by a daily job on the backend. The reservation row itself is kept – date, number of guests, amount, payment gateway – because accounting needs it and …
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via the WordPress plugin directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu. 3. Go to mee-table -> Settings, paste your licence key (from your mee-table.com dashboard), and click Activate licence.
  3. Set up your location(s), opening hours and payment methods on the Locations and Settings pages. 5. Optional: to switch the guest assistant on, open mee-table -> Guest assistant and paste a Groq key. Until you do, nothing is sent anywhere and the chat does not appear.
sections.faq:
Where should my Google Business Profile booking link point?

To your dedicated booking page, not to your homepage, even if the widget is on the homepage too. A link always opens at the top of a page: on a long homepage the guest lands on the header and has to scroll to find the widget, on the booking page they land right on it. The plugin creates that page for you (see mee-table -> Settings) and the floating booking pill brings guests there from every other page of your site.

Does mee-table store guest data on my WordPress server?

On the free Lite plan, reservations stay in the restaurant owner’s WordPress database. On plans with an active mee-table licence, booking data is stored on the mee-table server (api.mee-table.com).

Does the AI guest assistant cost anything, and is it on by default?

It is off until you paste a Groq API key in mee-table -> Guest assistant, and while that field is empty the plugin contacts no AI service at all and the chat is not even loaded on your pages. The key is free to create at https://console.groq.com/keys and the account is yours, so the free allowance is yours alone and the plugin never resells anything.

What does the assistant tell guests about allergens?

If you have ticked your menu page and the answer is written there, it repeats what you wrote and says it read it from you. What it never does is promise a guest that a dish is safe for their own allergy: a question like “I am allergic to hazelnuts, can I eat this?” always goes to your phone, whatever your menu says. Cross-contamination is decided in your kitchen, not on a menu, and only you know how you work.

And about prices?

The same rule. If your menu with prices is on a page you ticked, it can repeat a figure you wrote. If it is not published, it tells the guest to ask you. It never invents a figure, and it never says a percentage: on time-slot discounts it tells the guest which times are discounted and that they are marked on the list, so the number is read from your own page and cannot be misquoted.

The admin panel is in the wrong language. Where do I change it?

By default the panel follows Settings -> General -> Site Language. If you want it pinned to one language regardless, set it in mee-table -> Settings -> Panel language.

Do you take a commission on my bookings?

No. Table reservations never carry a commission, on any plan, including the free one. A percentage applies only to tickets sold and paid online: Dating Aperitivo is 20% free, 15% Bronze, 12% Silver, 10% Gold; Cooking Class tickets go 12% free, 5% Bronze, 3% Silver, 2% Gold; gift cards are 10% free, 5% on every paid plan. It is taken at the moment of payment; the rest reaches your own Mollie, Stripe or PayPal account directly. Sell no tickets and you pay no percentage.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

It stays. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins page keeps your reservations, your customers, your venues, your time slots, your discounts and your hourly capacity: install it again and they are all still there. Only what the plugin generated by itself is cleaned up, such as caches and counters. If you really do want everything gone, there is a switch in mee-table -> Settings, off to begin with, that has to be turned on first. With it on the deletion is immediate and there is no undo, so only a backup of your site would bring anything back.

Where can I manage my licence or upgrade?

Log into your dashboard at https://mee-table.com/dashboard. There you can manage your location(s), billing, and staff accounts.

Why does the plugin need to connect to api.mee-table.com?

The connection is required for the booking widget, payment processing, and no-show protection to work. Without it, Mee-Table cannot retrieve availability, process payments, or update reservations.

What is the difference between the no-show guarantee and the prepayment tiers?

They are two different things, each with its own refund setting. The no-show guarantee only authorises the card: no money is taken, so there is nothing to refund. Its setting is a deadline, up to when the guest may cancel without a penalty. The prepayment tiers take real money at booking time, for a fixed-price menu you have already shopped for: that setting decides whether it is refundable at all, and defaults to non-refundable. A venue can run a flexible guarantee alongside a non-refundable tasting menu, which a single shared setting made impossible.

I set up an SMS provider. How do I know the credentials are right?

Use the “Send test SMS” button under the credentials. It sends one real message, using what is typed in the form even if you have not saved yet, and it costs one credit of your plan. Missing fields are reported before anything is dispatched, and the button locks for ten seconds after each attempt so a double click cannot burn credits. Note that the test leaves from your own site while real reminders leave from the mee-table servers: if your provider filters by IP address, the test can succeed where real sending fails.

What photo should I use for a cooking class?

A horizontal one, and as large as you can. The picture sits in a wide band on the flyer and in the email, so a portrait shot only shows a central strip of itself. When you pick the file the plugin crops it to 3:2, tells you which print sizes that photo can actually carry (A3 needs about 2200 px of width, A4 about 1550) and compresses it below 600 KB before it leaves your computer, so the 15 MB a modern phone produces is never uploaded. No compression invents pixels that were never there: a small photo stays small.

Which paper size should I print the flyer on?

A3 for a poster read from a distance, A4 for a window or a wall, A5 for a table stand, portrait or landscape. Each size is laid out separately rather than being a scaled copy, because what makes text readable is the distance it is read from, not the size of the sheet. The flyer always shows the next scheduled event: if nothing is scheduled it says so instead of printing a date that has passed.

Can a guest give a gift card to someone else? Does it arrive on WhatsApp?

Yes. The buyer can add the recipient’s name, email and phone. If they add the email, mee-table emails the gift card to the recipient right after payment. The buyer can also choose the day the email goes out (“Send on”), from tomorrow up to a year ahead, for example for a birthday: it is sent that morning at 9:00. If they leave the email empty, the gift card reaches only the buyer, who then has to send it separately. After payment a window opens with a green “Share on WhatsApp” button: WhatsApp opens with the message ready (amount, venue, code and link) and the buyer taps send. The WhatsApp message is not sent automatically and cannot be scheduled. If the buyer typed the recipient’s phone it is already filled in; if not, the number can be typed in that window. They can also add a personal message of up to 200 characters, which the recipient reads in the email. Gift cards are paid with Mollie or Stripe Connect, whichever the venue has connected.

Can I have different sittings on different days?

Yes. In mee-table → Location, edit the location and open the first tab, Venue, hours & booking confirmation: right after the opening hours you find Rates by time slot / custom shifts (the ? next to the title opens the guide). Add one row per sitting with + Add tier, then Save the rates only, tick its days and set its time. Example: three rows at 20:00, 21:45 and 23:00 ticked Fri, Sat and Sun, and other rows for Tue, Wed and Thu. Type any start time you like, for example 20:05 or 21:45: the sitting times do not depend on the time interval, which only sets the grid of the normal times for the whole location (every 30 or every 15 minutes). Tick “One time for the sitting” to show a single button per sitting, or choose “Show only the times of the tiers” to hide the normal grid. A row with an empty amount or 0 has no prepayment; the no-show guarantee (from Silver), if you keep it on, still applies. Sittings without an amount work on every plan, Free included; prepayment amounts are part of the Gold plan, and below Gold the amount field is switched off with a note.

Can I close at different times during the week, for example earlier on weekdays than on weekends?

Yes, with the same sittings, and it holds for good until you change it. In mee-table → Location, edit the location, first tab, Rates by time slot / custom shifts. Switch on Show only the times of the tiers below and add one row for each group of days with different hours. Set From to the first bookable time and To to the last bookable time, leave the amount empty, and leave One time for the sitting unticked. Example: Mon to Thu from 12:00 to 22:00 (last bookable time 22:00) and Fri to Sun from 12:00 to 22:30 (last bookable time 22:30). Tick the days for each row, then Save the rates only. Guests see the times from From through To, including To, at the interval set for the location (every 30 or 15 minutes). A day with no row keeps the location’s normal opening hours and closing time; you do not need to add a row for every day. Discounts and hourly capacity stay tied to the times actually offered on each day. The quick blocks in the calendar (Hourly Capacity) are for single dates or a period, such as holidays, not for fixed weekly hours. With Show all normal times, the rows do not change the schedule: only the location’s normal opening hours and closing time count.

How do I enable the WhatsApp contact button?

Go to mee-table → Location, edit the location, and fill in the “WhatsApp (digits only)” field with the number in international format, digits only (e.g. an Italian number +39 333 123 4567 becomes 393331234567). Once saved, a WhatsApp chat button appears automatically under the booking widget on your site, linking to a direct chat with that number. This uses the free wa.me link: no paid service, no extra setup, available on every plan tier.
sections.changelog:
1.3.8

  • Fixed: on a phone the last bookings of the staff dashboard could not be reached. The window now scrolls as a whole and is sized on the visible part of the screen, without the browser bars.

1.3.7

  • Gift cards now have their own page in the panel: the full register of every card issued (buyer, recipient, value, remaining balance and the commission mee-table received), with free search and month and year filters, fifty rows at a time. It used to sit inside the Venues page, where it grew longer every month.
  • One CSV for your accountant: gift card sales and redemptions together, in date order, with the commission and, for every sale, buyer, recipient, remaining balance, status and expiry. It replaces the two separate exports.
  • New: fixed menus have their own refund choice on the Fixed menus page: non-refundable (the default) or refundable up to the number of hours before that you choose. It applies only to prepaid menus.
  • New: the link in the fixed menu emails opens the booking on your own menus page, not on mee-table.com. From there the guest can cancel, add or remove a menu (if not paid online) or change menu.
  • New: changing fixed menu. The guest books the new menu from your page and the old booking is cancelled only when the new one is confirmed or paid. If they had paid online, they pay only the difference for a more expensive menu, or get the difference back for a cheaper one when the menu is refundable and still within your hours; otherwise they are asked to call you.
  • Changed: gift card validity guidance in the panel: 18 months recommended (the usual period in most European countries), 24 months in the Netherlands; ask your accountant which validity to apply. New venues start at 18 months.
  • Fixed: the gift card fee note now says that the EUR 10 cap applies to paid plans and the trial, while the free plan is 10% with no cap.
  • Fixed: the “+ Add amount” button of the gift card amounts was translated as cropping an image in German, French, Spanish, Dutch and Portuguese.
  • Fixed: when mee-table.com cannot be reached, the course languages and the fixed menus try again after 5 minutes instead of on every page view, so your pages no longer wait for it each time.
  • The commission is read from the server, never estimated in the plugin: cards issued before 9 October 2026 have no commission recorded and are shown blank, not as a zero.
  • Fixed: on a site in Chinese (Traditional) or Korean the booking widget showed its own labels in English (Number of guests, Guests, Date, Time, Contact, and the payment terms), because those two languages had no dictionary in the plugin. They now have one, with the whole widget translated, including the payment terms and the card window.
  • The booking page, the Gift Card page and the Staff login page are now created in every language of the site when WPML or Polylang is active. Pages that already existed before this update are covered too: the translations are created the first time you open the panel after updating, so you do not have to save anything again.
  • Fixed: on a WPML or Polylang site the widget now follows the language of the page the guest is looking at, so the widget labels, the language switcher and the payment terms all agree.
  • New: each venue can switch its Gift Cards off. The button disappears from the booking widget and the purchase page, and the amounts you had saved stay there: switch it back on and everything is as before. It used to be all or nothing, and deleting the amounts was the only way to stop selling.
  • New: the custom Stripe and PayPal credentials of a venue can now be removed. Ticking the box and saving erases them from that venue, which goes back to the global keys; until now the fields could only be emptied, and the key stayed saved and in use.
  • New: staff can move a booking from the Floor Dashboard on the phone (button Move: pick the day, see the free times with the seats left, confirm). Each venue decides who can do it, all staff or managers only, in Locations > Staff; out of the box all staff can do it, like cancelling, and you can restrict it to managers. The guest receives the new time by email.
  • New: Stripe and PayPal with your own keys now work as a bridge for prepaid bookings. They are offered only until Mollie (verified) or Stripe Connect is active for the venue: from then on they switch off by themselves. Each one has its own on/off switch for the whole site (Settings) and for each venue (Locations > Payments); switching off never deletes your keys. Keep the keys until the prepaid bookings have taken place: they are needed to refund from the plugin.
  • The Global Mollie box was removed from Settings: every venue connects its own Mollie account, as it always had to.
  • Fixed: the Stripe and PayPal webhooks now acknowledge events that belong to other activities on the same account (a shop, a POS, other apps) instead of answering with an error. Before, Stripe could report the webhook as failing and switch it off after a few days.
  • New: a separate switch “Also on the courses page” (Settings, next to “Buttons in capitals, like my theme”). The courses page shows only mee-table buttons and keeps its own look by default; switch it on if you place it among other capital-letter buttons of your site.
  • Changed: the “Next Cooking Class” button of the booking widget now appears only when your site has a courses page (the page with the [mee-cooking] shortcode) and always opens it. It no longer sends guests to mee-table.com. The Dating button still opens the match page on mee-table.com.
  • New: the courses page ([mee-cooking]) is now created on your site by itself as soon as you have an active class, and only then (no classes, no page). The option “Create a page on my site for the classes” is on by default and you can switch it off. The plugin never deletes a page and does not recreate one you have removed.

1.3.6

  • Fixed: with a licence the menu showed both Bookings and the staff page. Bookings now appears only in the free Lite version, where it is the place to see reservations; with a licence you use the Floor Dashboard.
  • The staff page now has a gender-neutral name in every language (Floor Dashboard, Cruscotto sala, Panel de sala, Tableau de bord de salle, Service-Übersicht, Painel de sala).
  • Gift cards: each amount can now have an optional name (for example Bronze 100, Silver 150).
  • A short note next to the Stripe and PayPal credentials explains that PayPal is meant for the first days only, while Mollie or Stripe verify your account.
  • The no-show guarantee can now also use Stripe Connect, as an alternative to Mollie: each venue chooses. Mollie works exactly as before.
  • Gift cards: the buyer now chooses how the gift reaches the other person: by email, right away or on a chosen day (it arrives that morning at 9:00, in the venue’s own time zone), and on WhatsApp from their own phone.   • Gift cards can now also be sold with Stripe Connect, as an alternative to Mollie: each venue chooses, and the Gift Card button appears as soon as one of the two is connected. Mollie works exactly as before.

1.3.5

  • Fixed: the Bookings entry was missing from the mee-table menu, so clicking mee-table opened Locations and the list of reservations could not be reached. Bookings is back as the first entry.
  • Sittings without an amount (time slots that only decide which times guests can book) are now available on every plan. Prepayment amounts stay from the Gold plan, and when a plan does not include something the panel now says which plan does.
  • The “Rates by time slot / custom shifts” section has a clearer name and a short example, in all 9 languages.
  • Sittings without an amount now work in the free Lite version too, without a licence: they are saved in your WordPress site.
  • The “Rates by time slot / custom shifts” section has moved to the first tab of the location (“Venue, hours & booking confirmation”), right after the opening hours, with a ? link to the guide. The payments tab keeps a note that points there.
  • Dutch: the waiter dashboard is now the neutral “Bedieningsdashboard”.

1.3.4

  • Cooking class pages with WPML and Polylang: existing translated pages are linked instead of duplicated.
  • Class Presentation offers the site languages and “+ Add language”, same list as the set menus.
  • Class prices: adults from 10 EUR, children from 5 EUR.
  • Table deposits with Stripe: charged in the currency of your Stripe account, refund button works with Stripe too.
  • New “Test payment” button: a real 0.10 EUR payment to check bookings, emails and payouts.
  • New: sittings that change by day, each with its own start time, days, dates and optional prepayment, plus a time interval of 15 or 30 minutes for the whole venue.
  • New: gift cards on one page with a venue picker, gifting by email (on a day you choose, up to a year ahead) and a “Share on WhatsApp” button, and a “Coming soon” page while Mollie is not connected.
  • New: the widget follows your site: colours, the heading font of your theme and the month name of the calendar. Reading texts are dark for better contrast.
  • Changed: the booking page and the Gift Card page are created in every language of the site with WPML or Polylang.
  • Fixed: the confirm button no longer turns gold when the mouse goes over it.

1.3.3

  • New: you choose what your staff can do from the phone dashboard. For each venue, five switches decide who may confirm a booking, cancel it, mark a no-show, refund a payment and waive a no-show fee: all staff, or the manager only. Out of the box confirm, cancel and no-show are open to all staff, while refunds and waived fees stay with the manager. The buttons a person may not use are hidden, and the server refuses them too.
  • Fixed: the staff dashboard on the phone and the Waiter Dashboard in the panel are now the same dashboard, and show the same bookings. The phone one did not show set menus.
  • Fixed: set menus show their real name and price everywhere, in every language, instead of a generic “Special Menu” label in Italian.
  • Changed: the dashboards list tables and set menus only. Cooking class and event tickets have their own ticket list and the QR check at the door.

1.3.2

  • Fixed: time slots with a discount showed the time broken in two (“17:0” and “0”) when the booking form sits in a narrow column. The discount badge stays next to the time and is readable, and the time is never split: when there is not enough room for three columns the form switches to two, like on a phone, and to one in very narrow boxes. Time grids without discounts look exactly as before.
  • Fixed: in a very narrow column (about 280 to 320 pixels) the calendar and the third column of times went past the right edge of the form. They now stay inside.
  • Fixed: the set menu booking window went 17 pixels past the edge of the menu card in narrow columns on some themes.
  • Fixed: a free trial started from your mee-table.com account is now recognised by the plugin, so every feature is unlocked during the trial as promised.

1.3.1

  • Fixed: on the free plan the booking form ignored your opening hours and always offered 12:00 to 22:00. A restaurant that opens at 17:00 was taking bookings at lunchtime. It now follows the opening and closing time you saved, your lunch and dinner service windows and your weekly closing day, exactly like the paid plans already did. The last table offered is 30 minutes before closing.
  • Fixed: when the booking form sits inside a narrow column of a wide page, the step names (Guests, Date, Time, Contact) broke in the middle of the word. In a narrow box the form now shows the step numbers and the name of the current step only, and never splits a word. In a normal-size box it looks exactly as before.

  • New: deleting the plugin no longer deletes what you wrote. Your reservations, customers, venues, time slots, discounts and hourly capacity stay, and come back if you install it again. A switch in Settings, off to begin with, is there for anyone who really does want everything gone.
  • New: set menu booking now stays on your own website. The booking form opens inside the page, like the cooking class one already did, instead of sending the guest to mee-table.com: guests were calling the restaurant to ask whether the other website was genuine. Only the payment page itself still takes the whole window, because payment providers refuse to be shown inside a frame.
  • New: the waiter dashboard shows which set menu each guest bought, and a box at the top counts the portions per menu per service (day and time), which is how a kitchen actually prepares them.

  • New: the little “?” that opens the guide is now next to every section, not only next to the page title. Forty-one of them across the panel, each one landing on the paragraph that explains that section.
  • Fixed: the “?” links and the new Guide entry open the guide in the language of your panel. They always opened the Italian one, whatever language you were working in.

  • New: the set menu booking form is no longer English only.   • Fixed: “Back to all menus”, inside the booking form, showed a broken grey box instead of going back. It now closes the form and puts you back on the list, which is right there on the page.
  • Fixed: the day separator row in the waiter dashboard stopped one column short when a payment column was showing.
  • Fixed: on a multilingual site (WPML or Polylang) renaming your set menus page could rename one of the translations instead of the page you were looking at, leaving the others untouched. The plugin now always works on the page in the language you are in.
  • New: “Buttons in capitals, like my theme”, next to the theme font option, for themes that write every button in capitals. And if you already asked mee-table to follow your theme’s font, it now follows the theme’s capitals too, without switching anything on.
  • Changed: the panel entry is now called “Set Menus”, not “Special Menus”. In English this has always been a set menu, the fixed-price lunch, and the page, the button and this readme already said so: only the menu entry did not. Nothing you wrote is affected, and any page already created keeps working.

  • The waiter dashboard breaks the list by day, with the day written once and the guest count next to it, and today’s rows stand out. Each row carries a colour stripe for its status, and the whole table fits on the screen again. Refunding moved in with the other buttons, where it belongs, and only shows up when there is something to refund.

  • Fixed: the set menu confirmation email gave the day but not the time.
  • Fixed: lines written one under the other at the end of a set menu description ran together into a single block on your website. They now break where you wrote them.

short_description: Free Lite version: restaurant reservations, table booking and event tickets on your own site. Gift cards and no-show protection need an account.
description:
mee-table lets you accept table reservations from your own WordPress site, with a booking calendar, capacity per time slot and a confirmation email to the guest.

Free, with no account and no key. Reservations, the booking calendar, basic capacity, the confirmation email and events with ticket sales all run on your own WordPress, in your own database, using your own site email address. Nothing to sign up for, nothing to pay.

This is the Lite version, and it is free forever. With a mee-table account you also get prepayments and no-show protection (card or digital wallet), gift cards, the guest assistant, WhatsApp and SMS reminders, time-based discounts, staff accounts with the Waiter Dashboard, reports, and colours that match your theme. These run through the mee-table service at api.mee-table.com, so there is no server for you to maintain.

Every installation starts with a 14-day trial of the full version. When the trial ends the plugin does not switch off: it carries on at the free level, and your venues and bookings stay where they are.

What it costs, and what we take. The plugin is free. A mee-table account is from EUR 24 per month billed yearly (EUR 29 monthly), and there are higher plans for larger venues and groups.

We never take a commission on table reservations. Ever, on any plan, including the free one. A guest booking a table costs you nothing.

A percentage applies only where a ticket is sold and paid online: Dating Aperitivo tickets, Cooking Class tickets and gift cards. It is deducted at the moment of payment, and the rest goes straight to your own Mollie, Stripe or PayPal account. Mollie only opens accounts for businesses based in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the United Kingdom (list of countries); venues elsewhere, for example in the US, connect Stripe:

  • Free (or after the trial ends): 20% on Dating Aperitivo, 12% on Cooking Class, 10% on gift cards
  • Bronze: 15% on Dating Aperitivo, 5% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Silver: 12% on Dating Aperitivo, 3% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Gold: 10% on Dating Aperitivo, 2% on Cooking Class, 5% on gift cards
  • Platinum: agreed with you

On paid plans and during the trial the gift card percentage is capped at EUR 10 per card; on the free plan it is 10% with no cap.

Both percentages go down as you move up a plan: Dating Aperitivo from 20% on Free to 10% on Gold, Cooking Class from 12% to 2%. If you never sell a ticket, you never pay a percentage.

Main features:

  • Table reservations with availability, opening hours, rules on the number of guests, a weekly closing day and a quick-block calendar for one-off closures.
  • Guests manage their booking on YOUR site. The link in every email and message opens your own booking widget, on your own pages, in edit mode: the guest moves the date, the time or the number of guests, or cancels, inside the limits you set. A per-venue cap says how many people one booking may bring (the venue capacity is a separate number), and an optional notice window closes online changes some hours before the table, after which the guest is asked to call you.
  • Move a booking instead of losing it. The guest can change the day, the time or the number of people from the link in their confirmation email, without calling: the free tables are re-checked live, and you decide how many times they may do it before they are asked to phone you. Your own staff can move any booking from the Waiter Dashboard, with no limit, the phone rings there.
  • Your own time zone, so opening hours and reminders are right even when the venue and the server are in different countries.
  • Prepayment by time band. An “Aperitivo” rate from 19:00 to 20:00 and a different one for dinner, each with its own days of the week and minimum number of guests. The guest is only ever offered the rate that covers the time they picked, and when a rate covers it the prepayment replaces the no-show card guarantee: nobody is asked to pay twice for the same evening.
  • Sittings that change by day. For example 20:00, 21:45 and 23:00 from Friday to Sunday, and other times from Tuesday to Thursday. You type the start time you want, even 20:05. A sitting with no amount (for example Aperitivo 18:00-20:00, Dinner 20:00-22:00, After-dinner 22:00-24:00) only decides which times guests can book, and works on every plan, Free included and without a licence, because it is saved in your WordPress site. Prepayment amounts start from the Gold plan (or the 14-day trial).
  • Gift cards paid with Mollie or Stripe Connect, with a “Coming soon” preview per venue, a venue picker, one page per language with WPML or Polylang, and gifting to another person by email or WhatsApp.
  • Choose which emails reach you. Everything that happens to a booking sends you an email by default, confirmed, declined, cancelled or moved, including what your own staff did from the dashboard. Untick the ones you do not want; your guests keep receiving theirs either way.
  • No-show guarantee: the guest’s card is authorised, not charged. Nothing is taken unless they fail to turn up, and staff release or charge it from the Waiter Dashboard.

  • You decide what your staff can do. For each action on the phone dashboard (confirm, cancel, mark a no-show, refund a payment, waive a no-show charge) you choose all staff or the manager only. Until you change it, everything works as before.

  • Set menus at a fixed price, that guests book like a ticket: the whole thing happens on YOUR website, from the list of menus to the booking form, and only the payment page itself opens the payment provider’s own window, because they refuse to be shown inside a frame. You can ask for full prepayment, cap the seats per day or per service, and write each menu in as many languages as you like. The kitchen sees how many portions per service in the Waiter Dashboard.

  • Cooking classes, custom events and Dating Aperitivo, each with its own page on your site, its own photo, its own ticket and its own flyer to print.

External services

The city pages on mee-table.com (off by default)

Under mee-table, Events, Cooking Classes, Presentation there is a tick called “Show this class on the mee-table.com page for your city”. It is off unless you turn it on. With it on, the title, the description, the photo, the address and the next dates of your class appear on our public city page, for example https://mee-table.com/corsi-di-cucina/firenze, so people searching for a cooking class in your town can find you. Untick it and you are off that page at the next save. Nothing else about your venue is published.

This plugin relies on external services. Below is what each one is, when it is contacted, and what is sent to it.

1. mee-table backend (https://api.mee-table.com): always required

The plugin is a client for the mee-table SaaS. Every page of the admin and every booking talks to it. Data sent: reservation details (guest name, email, phone, number of guests, date, notes), location configuration, prepayment and gift-card records, staff accounts, and any photo you upload for a cooking class. Without this service the plugin cannot show availability, take payments or store bookings. Provided by mee-table. Terms: https://mee-table.com/terms | Privacy: https://mee-table.com/privacy

Two calls to the same provider happen outside the admin pages, and are listed here separately so it is clear when they occur:

  • Activating the plugin sends nothing anywhere. The first contact happens when you enter your licence key and press Activate: at that moment, once, the plugin asks https://mee-table.com/api/provisioning whether this domain already has a mee-table account, so the site connects to its own restaurant without anyone typing a token. Data sent: the site URL (get_site_url()) and nothing else. If it fails, the plugin simply carries on unconfigured. Until a licence key is entered, the plugin contacts no server at all.
  • Once a day, a scheduled task asks https://api.mee-table.com/api/license/validate whether the subscription is still active. Data sent: the site URL, the licence key the site owner entered, and the name of the product asking (mee-table), so a key bought for mee-class does not unlock bookings. How that data is handled: https://mee-table.com/privacy This call does not happen at all until a licence key has been entered: with no key the task returns immediately.

No guest data is involved in either of these two calls.

2. Payment providers: only when you enable and connect them

Mollie, Stripe or PayPal are contacted to create payments, authorise no-show guarantees and issue refunds. Data sent: amount, currency, reservation reference, and the guest’s payment details entered on the provider’s own hosted page. Card numbers never pass through WordPress. Mollie: https://www.mollie.com/en/user-agreement | https://www.mollie.com/en/privacy Stripe: https://stripe.com/legal | https://stripe.com/privacy PayPal: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/home

3. SMS providers: only if you choose one, and only for the messages you send

If you configure an SMS provider, your site sends the reminder text and the guest’s phone number to it. Two paths exist: reminders are dispatched by the mee-table backend, while the “Send test SMS” button sends one message directly from your own WordPress server to the provider, using the credentials you typed in. Nothing is sent to any of these companies unless you select them and save credentials. The panel also accepts a custom HTTP gateway: in that case the same two pieces of data go to the endpoint address you type in yourself, and to nobody else.

Twilio: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal Skebby (Commify Italia S.r.l.): terms https://www.skebby.it/wp-content/uploads/Contratto-SKEBBY.pdf | privacy https://www.skebby.it/wp-content/uploads/Informativa-Privacy-Estesa-SKEBBY.pdf Aruba SMS: https://hosting.aruba.it/documents/term_conditions/condizioni_fornitura_servizisms_aruba-it_v-1-2.aspx | https://www.aruba.it/documents/tc-files/it/11_it_privacy_policy_aruba_spa.aspx Brevo: https://www.brevo.com/legal/ Vonage: https://www.vonage.com/legal/ (its SMS endpoint is still the old brand name, https://rest.nexmo.com)

SMSGate (https://api.sms-gate.app): only if you choose the Android phone gateway

If you pick “Android phone” as the SMS route, your site does not talk to the phone directly: it sends the reminder text and the guest’s phone number to the SMSGate cloud at https://api.sms-gate.app/3rdparty/v1, which passes the message to the free SMSGate app on your own phone, and the message then leaves from your own SIM. This happens only for the messages you send, and only after you have installed the app and saved its username and password in the panel. SMSGate is an open-source project (the app is at https://github.com/capcom6/android-sms-gateway) and the cloud service is run by its authors.

SMSGate: https://sms-gate.app/terms-of-service/ | https://sms-gate.app/privacy/

A “generic HTTP” option exists for providers not in the list: there the endpoint is the one you type in, and you are responsible for it.

4. Meta / WhatsApp Business Cloud API (https://graph.facebook.com): only if you set up WhatsApp messages

If you fill in the WhatsApp fields of a location (phone number ID, WhatsApp Business Account ID and access token, all obtained from your own Meta Business account), your WordPress site talks to Meta directly in three cases, and never otherwise:

  • “Create the message templates on Meta”: reads the message templates that already exist on your WhatsApp Business Account and submits the missing ones for Meta’s approval. Data sent: the wording of the booking messages and your access token. No guest data.
  • “Send test WhatsApp”: sends one real confirmation message, filled with sample values, to the number you type into that field, to check the setup works. Data sent: that phone number, the sample values and your access token. No guest data.
  • The reminder texts themselves are fetched from https://mee-table.com/api/whatsapp/modelli, a public page of the mee-table site that only returns the wording of those messages. Nothing is sent to it.

The WhatsApp Business Account is yours: you own the number and you pay Meta directly. mee-table neither resells messages nor owns any number. Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-terms | Privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-data-processing-terms Meta Platform Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms | Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy

5. Mailchimp: only if you enter an API key

Used to add newsletter subscribers to your audience. Data sent: the email address and the consent flag of guests who opted in. https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/ | https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/

6. Groq: only if you enter a Groq API key for the guest assistant

Used by the guest assistant on your booking page. When a visitor types a question, that question is sent, together with your restaurant’s public information (name, address, phone, opening times, which time slots are still free in the next 7 days, discounts and events), to Groq, which produces the answer. The request is made server-to-server through the mee-table backend using your own Groq account, so the key never appears in a public page.

Never sent: names, phone numbers or e-mail addresses of your guests, and no booking of theirs. Free seats are counted; who booked them is not sent.

Nothing at all is sent to Groq unless you have entered a key in mee-table -> Guest assistant. Leaving that field empty keeps the assistant off and the script is not even loaded. Groq does not retain these questions for inference requests and is not permitted to use them to train its models.

Getting a key is free and takes about two minutes at https://console.groq.com/keys, the plugin explains the steps on that settings page. The Groq account is yours: the agreement for it is between you and Groq. Terms: https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/services-agreement Privacy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy Acceptable use: https://console.groq.com/docs/legal/ai-policy

Answers are generated by an automated system and can be wrong, and the assistant tells the visitor that it is automatic. Any answer containing a percentage is discarded before the visitor sees it. An answer containing an amount is discarded too, unless you have published prices on the pages you ticked and that exact figure appears there: the assistant repeats what you wrote, it never composes a price. On allergens it answers only by repeating what your own pages say, and any request for a guarantee about a guest’s own health is sent to your phone instead.

Privacy

This plugin sends reservation data, prepayment details, gift-card information, and location configuration to the mee-table backend at https://api.mee-table.com. If you enable the WhatsApp reminders, the guest’s phone number is also sent to Meta’s WhatsApp Business Cloud API so the message can be delivered, using the WhatsApp Business Account that belongs to you. The data is used solely to provide the booking service, payment processing, and no-show protection. No data is sold, shared with third parties for marketing, or used for advertising. If you enable the guest assistant, visitors’ questions and your restaurant’s public information are sent to Groq through your own Groq account, as described under External services above; no guest personal data is included. For full details, please read the mee-table Privacy Policy.

Retention: identifying data on a reservation (guest name, email, phone and notes) is irreversibly erased 180 days after the reservation date, by a daily job on the backend. The reservation row itself is kept – date, number of guests, amount, payment gateway – because accounting needs it and …
